{
  "candidate_rtl": "module crc32_d8 (
    input  wire [7:0]  data_in,
    input  wire [31:0] state_in,
    output wire [7:0]  data_out,
    output wire [31:0] state_out
);
    // Common byte-wide input syndrome.
    wire [7:0] q;
    assign q = data_in ^ state_in[7:0];

    // Feedback bits emitted during the eight reflected Galois steps.
    assign data_out[5:0] = q[5:0];
    assign data_out[6] = q[6] ^ q[0];
    assign data_out[7] = q[7] ^ q[1];

    // Constant elaboration-time computation of each syndrome-to-state row.
    function automatic [7:0] row_mask;
        input integer bit_index;
        reg [31:0] c;
        integer j, t;
        begin
            row_mask = 8'b0;
            for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin
                c = 32'h00000001 << j;
                for (t = 0; t < 8; t = t + 1) begin
                    if (c[0])
                        c = (c >> 1) ^ 32'hedb88320;
                    else
                        c = c >> 1;
                end
                row_mask[j] = c[bit_index];
            end
        end
    endfunction

    function automatic integer population;
        input [7:0] mask;
        integer j;
        begin
            population = 0;
            for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1)
                population = population + (mask[j] ? 1 : 0);
        end
    endfunction

    function automatic integer selected_bit;
        input [7:0] mask;
        input integer ordinal;
        integer j, seen;
        begin
            selected_bit = 0;
            seen = 0;
            for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin
                if (mask[j]) begin
                    if (seen == ordinal)
                        selected_bit = j;
                    seen = seen + 1;
                end
            end
        end
    endfunction

    genvar b, k;
    generate
        for (b = 0; b < 32; b = b + 1) begin : output_row
            localparam [7:0] MASK = row_mask(b);
            localparam integer COUNT = population(MASK);
            wire [15:0] leaf;
            wire [7:0] level1;
            wire [3:0] level2;
            wire [1:0] level3;

            // Pack only actual operands before building a balanced XOR tree.
            // The shifted state bit participates in the same tree.
            for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : operands
                if (k < COUNT) begin : syndrome_term
                    localparam integer INDEX = selected_bit(MASK, k);
                    assign leaf[k] = q[INDEX];
                end else if ((k == COUNT) && (b < 24)) begin : shifted_state
                    assign leaf[k] = state_in[b+8];
                end else begin : padding
                    assign leaf[k] = 1'b0;
                end
            end
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1) begin : first_level
                assign level1[k] = leaf[2*k] ^ leaf[2*k+1];
            end
            for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : second_level
                assign level2[k] = level1[2*k] ^ level1[2*k+1];
            end
            for (k = 0; k < 2; k = k + 1) begin : third_level
                assign level3[k] = level2[2*k] ^ level2[2*k+1];
            end
            assign state_out[b] = level3[0] ^ level3[1];
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The supplied critical paths combine input buffering, substantial input-dependent XOR logic, and final parity reconstruction. Independently expressing parity over raw data and state bits can obscure their common byte syndrome and increase input loading.",
  "rewrite": "Specialize the reflected CRC32 update around q = data_in XOR state_in[7:0]. Generate the constant linear transformation of q using polynomial 0xedb88320, then implement each state output as a packed, explicitly balanced XOR tree including its shifted-state operand. Preserve data_out as the eight emitted feedback bits, including its two nontrivial feedback corrections. All functions and loops used for mask generation are elaboration-time computations.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The intended gain comes from exposing the common input syndrome and bounding parity-tree depth rather than retaining separate raw-input parity cones. Improvement over the supplied 0.98 ns baseline is plausible but unmeasured; no mapped timing, SAT, or electrical-check tools were available here, so no numerical gain or signoff result is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Eight syndrome XORs are shared across all outputs; constant-zero tree branches disappear during synthesis. Sharing should reduce duplicated parity work, but syndrome fanout may require buffering. Compliance with the 2752.64 um^2 cap and zero electrical violations requires measurement in the specified mapping flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The top-level name, port widths, and directions are preserved. The design is purely combinational and retains all 40 outputs for arbitrary values of all 40 inputs. It assumes no initialization, framing, reset, inversion, or gating. data_out[5:0] equals q[5:0], data_out[6] equals q[6] XOR q[0], and data_out[7] equals q[7] XOR q[1]. Only the specified fixed CRC32 instance is implemented. Native-source and mapped SAT equivalence remain required before acceptance."
}
